1:_: Seif 1, a place that has three partitions — see in my Chiburei Sefer HaChayim what is written regarding the law of eruvin on the words of Terumat HaDeshen; and see in siman 363 in my Chiburei Laws of Orach Chayim from the year 5599 in a responsum to the holy community of Zlotshev what is written to a certain sage who did not understand our words, and I explained there with God's help, examine well; and behold regarding the law whether a river is judged as a partition see what is written in my responsum to the holy community of Lutzka briefly in my Chiburei Laws of Even HaEzer laws of gittin siman 129 incidentally and it applies here, see in the responsum siman 285 and examine; and behold regarding the law whether tzurat hapetach helps when distant three tefachim from the wall see what is written somewhat in a responsum to Yoreh De'ah laws of bekhor in my Chiburei siman 58 incidentally to the holy community of Chernovil, see there and examine; and behold regarding what requires study in the sugya in the first chapter of Eruvin daf 11 regarding the law of tzurat hapetach that one made from the side see in my Chiburei to Yoreh De'ah siman 95 what is written there on this with God's help, examine well:
2:_: (There in seif 11) Even if he did not make it for the sake of lechi, etc., provided they relied on it on erev Shabbat, etc. Behold I was asked regarding the law of tzurat hapetach that they erected on Shabbat a reed with ropes — whether it is permitted to carry even though they did not rely on it on erev Shabbat; behold in my opinion the matter is simple and clear that it is permitted to carry and we do not require that they relied on it — only for lechi where there is no new recognition now and new making, and behold it is as it was yesterday, therefore we require that they relied on it on erev Shabbat; but for tzurat hapetach which is recognizable that it is an opening — not to mention if they erected the lechi and ropes on it now, certainly it is permitted, for it is not applicable to say that they did not rely on it on erev Shabbat since there is here great recognition that they erected it today; also even if the lechi stood from yesterday and now they tied the ropes on it — also permitted since we see that it is an opening, we do not require that they relied; and what the Taz wrote at the end of this siman — there it is different for the rope is not placed on the projections but only above and it is not true tzurat hapetach but only to combine it in our minds in place of lechi — here since it stood here from erev Shabbat and also is not placed on it but only above, here we require that they relied on it on erev Shabbat; but where they made it anew on Shabbat, even though the rope is above, or it was already there and they placed the rope on it in a manner that it is like a true opening — in this certainly we do not require that they relied on it on erev Shabbat, and so it appears correct in my humble opinion since it was made like a true opening we do not require that they relied on it on erev Shabbat, and so it appears and examine well:
3:_: (There in seif 26) That which a mavo is permitted by lechi or korah, etc., and its width should not be more than ten amot precise. Behold this is a dispute in the first chapter of Eruvin — Abbaye holds that amot of a mavo and amot of a sukkah are in amot of a daughter of five, and Rava holds in amot of a daughter of six only precise; and behold the Ra'osh wrote there that the halacha follows Rava, for Abbaye's matter we establish like Rashbag and Rava's matter like all — and I wondered why he needed this proof, for behold it is explicit in the Talmud that everywhere the halacha follows Rava against Abbaye except yod ayin lamed kuf gimmel mem; and one cannot say that this means only in Torah matters and not in rabbinic matters — this is not so, for behold here Rava is lenient and if so all the more in rabbinic matters the halacha follows Rava to be lenient; and further behold in yod ayin lamed kog gimmel mem it deals with lechi standing by itself and thus it is proved that also in rabbinic matters this rule applies; also I saw there in the Ra'osh letter dalet that he discusses whether the halacha follows Rav Yosef who is Abbaye's teacher or Abbaye, and it is implied that he holds that what we rule halacha follows the later ones from Abbaye and Rava onward — Abbaye and Rava themselves are not included; and see in my Chiburei Nedarim Zerizin siman 207 seif 18 where I brought there in the name of the Bach to the contrary, and in my Chiburei Sefer HaChayim siman 258 — and it is astonishing that these words of the early ones brought in the Ra'osh here were hidden from them; requires study. Further I saw that the question I asked on the Ra'osh — why not according to the reason that the halacha is not like Abbaye because Abbaye is only like Rashbag and Rava like all, and behold otherwise Abbaye and Rava — halacha follows Rava except yod ayin lamed kuf gimmel mem — the Knesset HaGedolah sensed this and strained in it; and in my humble opinion one may say more correctly: behold Rava said these are amot and Rashi explained amot precise, and accordingly one may say that this sign of yod ayin lamed kuf gimmel mem — the ayin hints at amot or the mem from kuf gimmel mem hints at precise — and thereby the halacha follows Abbaye; and one may say that certainly here the halacha follows Abbaye and it is yod ayin lamed kuf gimmel mem from what the Talmud ruled in ed zomem in Bava Kamma and mumar eating nevelot in Sanhedrin like Abbaye — one may say the Talmud was received that the halacha follows Abbaye in yod ayin lamed kuf gimmel mem and was itself uncertain whether the ayin hints at amot; but in ed zomem the halacha is not like Abbaye, or conversely the ayin hints at ed zomem and only the mem hints at precise, and in mumar the halacha is not like Abbaye; and since it is uncertain to him we rule according to both stringently like Abbaye who is stringent in both; but always one may say that amot here is one of the signs yod ayin lamed kuf gimmel mem and especially since it is to be stringent, therefore the Ra'osh wrote that here it is reasonable that the halacha is not like Abbaye since it is like a tannaitic dispute and therefore this is not yod ayin lamed kuf gimmel mem — and it comes out well thus it appears to speak on behalf of the Ra'osh, and this is easier than their strains — examine well; and behold when I was on this it was difficult for me in what they said both Abbaye and Rava that in sukkah where it is to be stringent it was a daughter of five or it is precise — and everything since it is to be stringent; and it is difficult, for behold we say in Sukkah chapter 3 regarding R' Yehuda who says a sukkah is enjoyed only with the four species of the lulav a fortiori, and they said there the Rabbis: any law whose beginning is to be stringent and its end to be lenient — there is no law; if he did not find four species he would sit idle, etc.; if so it is proved that this stringency is a leniency; if so here too it is a leniency if he has no sukkah except with a bent side of four amot precise or height twenty precise; if so if we say it is invalid and he has no other he would sit idle; if so this stringency is a leniency — and how did he say it is to be stringent, behold it is a stringency that leads to a leniency; and granted in a mavo it is only a stringency for otherwise he would not carry in it and he has no other; and one cannot say that granted there where it speaks from Torah law — if from Torah law it is not a sukkah except with four species, then even if he has no other he is exempt from sitting in this one, therefore it is considered a stringency that leads to a leniency; but here which is only rabbinic — if so in truth if he has no other he sits in this one and therefore it is not a stringency that leads to a leniency; but if so why does the Talmud challenge that it is a leniency within four amot, and for one answer they do not hold that it speaks of most amot — it should have challenged more, for behold in height and bent side there is also leniency if he has no other whether he is obligated to sit in this one or not — then we measure in an amah of a daughter of six and perforce we must say it speaks of most amot; if so it is difficult for the one who does not hold it speaks of most amot — requires study, examine well. And see in my Chiburei Laws of Orach Chayim from the year 5601 in the first chapter laws of Chanukah siman 471 what is written there regarding korah — whatever part of it is within twenty or near twenty amah, as long as the hollow is only twenty — even if you lean it upward the lower one does not suffice and it would fall, nevertheless it is valid since in the end now it stands, it becomes like iron skewers; but in s'chach it is not so — only here if you lean it upward the lower one's shade would not be greater from itself it is invalid — not like Ran whom the Taz brought in siman 633, see there, a matter in its reason for it is good with God's help, examine well: (There) And if it was higher than twenty and he built a structure beneath the korah to reduce below twenty — a structure one tefach wide suffices in the width of the korah, etc. Behold what is written that it should be higher than twenty — the intent perforce is that it refers to the hollow, for the hollow is higher than twenty and not the korah, for behold the Shulchan Aruch ruled above that the hollow of a mavo we learned as is written explicitly in this seif, and if the hollow was higher than twenty, etc.; if so since here it deals that the hollow is more than twenty — why did he write afterward and he built a structure beneath the korah to reduce below twenty — it would be enough to reduce from more than twenty until twenty it is valid; from this it appears clearly that his intent is as the Maggid Mishneh wrote in s.k. 7 — it appears from the words of the Rif and R' Yonatan beginning of Eruvin that if initially it was above twenty and he comes to reduce it he places the korah so that it is also part of the twenty; but if it is not high above twenty only the korah — he need not reduce it for this purpose, perforce. And this that the Shulchan Aruch wrote precisely — first he wrote and if it was higher than twenty — meaning the hollow is more than twenty, for otherwise if the hollow was not more than twenty even though the korah is placed above twenty he would not need to reduce; but since the hollow is above twenty and if so he needs to reduce it — here he needs to reduce below twenty so that even twenty the hollow should not be only the korah should be within twenty; however it appears he need not reduce so much that the entire thickness of the korah should be within twenty — only enough to reduce somewhat from twenty so that somewhat of the korah is placed within twenty; and the reason appears: granted if the law were that the korah itself should be part of the twenty — then we require that the entire korah be within the twenty, for otherwise if you lean it — it would be a korah that was removed by wind and does not help; but according to us that we rule the hollow of a mavo we learned — then by law the entire korah may be above twenty, only therefore we require initially that the korah be within twenty lest he not be precise in measure and perhaps the hollow would be somewhat more than twenty and the korah invalid; therefore it is fit to be precise initially that the korah itself be within twenty and he not come to error in this — that if somewhat of the korah is placed within twenty there is no longer possibility of error that the hollow be more than twenty; and that the thickness of the korah is more than twenty we do not care, for in truth the entire korah is permitted above twenty for the hollow of a mavo we learned and it is not applicable to say it was removed; and therefore the Shulchan Aruch was precise and wrote that he built a structure to reduce below twenty and did not write how much to reduce according to the measure of the korah's thickness — perforce that with a slight reduction it suffices, and this is as we wrote that with somewhat of the korah that is within twenty it is permitted even initially. And with this is resolved what my friend the sharp rabbi R' Yisrael Bik asked to challenge the Maggid Mishneh's view from the Talmud Eruvin daf 3 side 2 — what is stated there that it challenges according to the one who says the hollow of a mavo we learned from what we learned how does he act — he places the korah from the edge of twenty and below, etc.; and why does it challenge — behold initially we require that the korah be within twenty and he did not say the hollow of a mavo we learned only for after the fact — and why does it challenge; and according to what we wrote it comes out very well, for behold Rashi explained there from the edge of twenty and below that the thickness of the korah should be within twenty — if so it challenges well: granted if the korah is part of the twenty — then we require that the entire thickness of the korah be part of the twenty; but if the hollow of a mavo we learned only initially it is fit that it be within twenty — here that if somewhat of the korah is within twenty and not the entire thickness of the korah — why require the entire thickness of the korah within the twenty; and what it answers there from the edge of twenty and above — the intent is not that until and not until is included and initially it is permitted to place the entire korah above twenty, only the intent is until and until is included that the korah should begin from the edge of twenty exactly and above so that part of the korah is placed at the edge of twenty and the length of its thickness goes above twenty — and this is exactly according to our view, examine well. However behold I examined again the language of Rabbeinu Yonatan beginning of Eruvin from which is the source of this law of the Maggid Mishneh — it is written there explicitly s.v. he places the korah, etc., that the entire thickness of the korah enters to complete twenty amah — and therefore the sharp rabbi's question remains in place; but the language of the Rif there does not bear even according to the Maggid Mishneh's view — this is the language of the Rif there how does he reduce it — he places upon it a korah from twenty and below, for where the hollow is twenty, end of his words — and it is language that has no explanation at all; and even according to the Maggid Mishneh's understanding there is no explanation that first it implies from his language that if he reduces he must reduce initially to be less than twenty and afterward he wrote for where the hollow is twenty — it implies he can make the reduction so its hollow is twenty — and his language contradicts itself; therefore it appeared clearly that a printing error fell in the Rif and it must read from twenty amah and above, for where the hollow is twenty; and also Rashi's view s.v. as much as he needs daf 4 side 2 is explicit there that enough initially to reduce so twenty hollow remains and not like the Maggid Mishneh's view. And behold to resolve Rabbeinu Yonatan's view it appeared — and also to resolve further what the sharp rabbi R' Yisrael Bik asked — why does it challenge on daf 4 it was high twenty amah and he came to reduce it how much does he reduce and it challenges as much as he needs — why does it challenge, let us say it challenges how much he reduces whether until twenty or more; but it appears certainly according to Rava himself who holds the hollow of a mavo we learned — even initially it is permitted to leave twenty of the hollow, only since Rabbah holds that the thickness of the korah is also part of the twenty — one may say this question how much does he reduce as much as he needs — Rav Yosef and Abbaye themselves who answer afterward are they themselves who asked thus, and like what Tosafos wrote in chapter 2 of Bava Metzia regarding and how much R' Yehuda in the first explanation, and in Beitzah daf 38 and in Nedarim likewise Rav Yosef and Abbaye themselves challenged thus — one may say they hold like Rabbah that with the korah it is twenty and do not hold like Rava, therefore since they and Rabbah hold thus and also for Rava the baraita that the Talmud challenges from it is difficult and must be emended — therefore the halacha follows Rava since he is later; and also since korah is rabbinic the halacha follows the lenient view — however this is specifically after the fact, but initially one should be concerned for Rabbah's view and his supporters and see that even the thickness of the korah be from the hollow of twenty in order to satisfy all views; but for Rava himself even initially we do not require that the korah be within twenty and it challenges well for Rava as in my humble opinion to explain Rabbeinu Yonatan's view; but since according to Rashi's view it is proved to the contrary and from the Rif also it is proved thus that there is a printing error in his words and it is proved he holds like Rashi — and this matter being rabbinic it appears we need not be concerned for this even initially as in my humble opinion here, examine well: Behold I said to copy here some questions necessary for practical law that I answered briefly. I was asked by the great rabbi R' Yoel Deutsch av beit din of Manistrishtsh regarding the eruv matter of the first chapter that was discussed — tzurat hapetach extended over several rooftops in a manner that the break between the middle houses — the lechi beneath the tzurat hapetach is not seen from this side and that, only the rope alone is seen — whether the eruv is valid; and this is because he saw in Tosafos Eruvin and the Ra'osh there in the section of ten of Rav — we require that the people of the mavo see tzurat hapetach, and in this case the middle ones do not see the entire tzurat hapetach. And this is what I answered: behold here there is no room for concern, for certainly it suffices that they see the tzurat hapetach above, and since they do not see the place — everyone knows there is a lechi from here and a lechi from here; and what he brought as proof from responsum of Panim Me'irot siman 144 and Sefer Mikveh HaMayim that tzurat hapetach does not help if they stand inside the house — behold this is not because it is not visible but the reason that a house is as one filled with water as is written there in Mikveh HaMayim explicitly; and what he questioned from the Talmud I settled this already in my novellae previously; and also even if the reason were because it is not visible — that is there where it is not visible at all from outside; but here since at least it is visible to some people it is no worse than visible from inside and equal from outside or conversely — it is judged as lechi and is not similar to a crooked mavo where tzurat hapetach is not seen at all. Further behold we do not make any correction in crookedness and rely that our mavo'ot have the law of courtyards as the Magen Avraham wrote siman 363 — if so the same here, there is no room for concern at all; and what he asked in the case where one lechi does not stand at the wall but near the windowsill — behold if the windowsill is not ten high it appears it does not help, for behold the main reason of the Tur is that it is a partition through which goats penetrate, and if so in the end goats can leap through there and the partition is nullified; therefore it appears fit to place it on the windowsill at the wall — and with this there is no room for concern at all, so I answered. Further I was asked regarding the law of tzurat hapetach that they erected on Shabbat a reed with ropes — whether it is permitted to carry even though they did not rely on it on erev Shabbat; and I answered: behold in my opinion the matter is simple and clear that it is permitted to carry and we do not require that they relied — only for lechi where there is no new recognition now and new making, and behold it is as it was yesterday, therefore we require that they relied on it on erev Shabbat; but for tzurat hapetach which is recognizable that it is an opening — not to mention if they erected the lechi and ropes on it now, certainly it is permitted; and what the Taz wrote at the end of this siman — there it is different; but where they made it anew on Shabbat — in this certainly we do not require that they relied on it on erev Shabbat; and it is correct in my humble opinion even though they wrote that the Peri Megadim is uncertain in this — in my opinion there is no room for concern and no place for doubt at all, and it is clear in my humble opinion since it was made like a true opening we do not require that they relied on it on erev Shabbat, examine well. Further I was asked by the rabbinical judge R' Yosef Kastinbrahn of the holy community of Kalmya recently — they came and corrected the city's eruvin in this manner: they make at both ends of the rope a wooden ring tied at each end and each ring is placed around the head of the lechi and the head of the lechi protrudes above those rings and the protrusion is visible to all, and the head of each lechi is grooved around it toward the outside from the rope so the ring can rest there and not fall down, end of the questioner's words. And I answered: he spoke well, for this is tzurat hapetach made from the side — why in his case, for the groove is outside and on the side of the rope there is no groove — here the entire rope and ring stand at the side of the lechi and not on it; only also even if the groove were on the side of the rope or grooved all around it — since the rope and ring are not on the lechi but on the ring and the ring is placed on the lechi — if so in the end the rope begins only from the side of the lechi and if so it is tzurat hapetach made from the side — what difference whether this side faces the street or this side faces the lechi opposite it; and between the lechayim also it does not help if it is at its side and not on it — therefore this is not a correction but a defect, and whoever adds detracts; and the essence is as the custom of the early ones and our custom, so I answered, examine well:
4:_: (Seif 29) A mavo whose one side ends at the sea, etc. See in the Taz what is written regarding frozen water that partitions are nullified and it is worse than garbage heap and is not in the category of a partition at all, as the Rambam wrote explicitly in his commentary chapter 8 of Ohalot that they melt quickly, see what is written there and examine: (There in the gloss) And there are those who disagree and hold that we are concerned lest the sea rise as a sandbar and there is no partition here. Behold the Taz expanded here in a responsum to forbid in all waters whose way is to freeze, similar to what we are concerned lest the sea rise as a sandbar — and the later rabbis in responsum of Emunat Shmuel and Chacham Tzvi and Knesset Yechezkel disagree and permit; and behold I have no time now to study this through analysis; but in brief it appears it is not similar to the concern lest the sea rise as a sandbar — for there it has no fixed time, therefore it is applicable to forbid on all Sabbaths of the year and on every Shabbat there is concern in this; but regarding freezing of water this is not common except in winter such as Tevet and Shevat and the like, but on other days and especially in summer days their way is not and it is impossible at all that they be frozen — therefore certainly we should not decree on summer days because of winter days since in summer days it is not common that they be frozen; and one cannot say we decree on summer Sabbaths because of winter — from where do we know to decree thus; and behold in truth the essence of the matter is rabbinic and it would be a decree on a decree — therefore we have only what the Sages said lest the sea rise as a sandbar — and that is where on this Shabbat itself there is this concern; but where on those Sabbaths it is not common we need not be concerned thus; one cannot say we decree on those Sabbaths because of others — from where do we have to say thus since we did not find this decree in the Talmud; and also even in winter days whose way is to be frozen and even when already frozen it appears the Taz's proofs are not proof — for all his proofs are from things that are not removed by themselves but only by a person, therefore one may say partitions are nullified; but frozen water behold is destined to melt by themselves and whatever stands by itself — therefore it is as if already done thus, therefore certainly they do not nullify partitions since it stands to melt by itself; and even though regarding irrigation we rule that frozen irrigation water is not considered irrigation water — see above laws of Netilat Yadayim siman 158 — nevertheless this is regarding it in itself, but in any case to be considered ground adjacent to be nullified on ground — in this even something that is not irrigation water if destined to be removed it does not nullify partitions; and if so here too — whatever its end is to melt by itself does not nullify a partition — thus it appears in my humble opinion to be lenient and rely on the view of those who permit, examine well; and see in my Chiburei on Orach Chayim from the year 5601 siman 409 in a responsum to the holy community of Barditchev what is written on this matter further with God's help, examine well; and further I was asked by the great sharp elder R' Yissachar av beit din of Shanstichov in the land of Poland regarding the bridges there, and thus he wrote: I ask one question regarding the bridges that great and mighty lords place and fish pass beneath them, also launderers are found there and sometimes people pass beneath the bridge, end of his question. Behold according to me there is no doubt this is not considered a partition — and what helps in this that fish pass beneath it and likewise people — this does not help except to nullify a partition through which goats penetrate, but to make a partition it does not help — for in the end since people also pass above, the public comes and nullifies the partition; and further I wonder at what he wrote regarding the ditch belonging to the country — who nullifies it — it is astonishing, as if this nullification requires that it be theirs — the intent is only whatever is breached and the public passes there the partition is nullified by itself and their intent is not needed; and behold in a partition through which goats penetrate — who nullifies the partition, and is there power in hand to nullify the partition — only by itself it is nullified; and also what he wrote regarding the ditch for garbage — I wonder at him how he did not sense, for behold regarding the sea we say lest the sea rise as a sandbar — it is proved that if the sea rises as a sandbar it nullifies the partition even though it is by itself and is not set for garbage — nevertheless if the public can pass there the partition is nullified; and likewise the Taz forbids where it can freeze in winter and the Magen Avraham who disagrees in any case forbids if the sea froze even though it belongs to the country and is not set for garbage — if so here too what difference whether it froze above or a bridge was made above and the public passes on it — whatever the public comes and nullifies the partition; and what difference whether it applies to an individual or the public or the entire country — by itself since the public penetrates it they nullify the partition. And also what he wrote regarding the sides of the bridge being coated with tar and an amaltara placed on them — he brought what is stated in Eruvin daf 11 that amaltara does not help in width — behold this too according to me is not so: one, that what is coated with tar does not have the law of amaltara — amaltara is when there are many designs and flowers; but what is coated with tar does not have the law of amaltara; and further amaltara only helps where there are partitions and lechi or korah only where it is wide more than ten in a manner that it is not like an opening — here regarding this the Talmud is uncertain whether amaltara helps in its width; but here in a bridge since there are no partitions and no korah and lechi — what relevance is amaltara here, especially according to the truth amaltara does not help in its width; and also what he wrote regarding amot — whether we require precise or imprecise — already see in the first chapter of Eruvin daf 3 that for eruvin to be stringent we require imprecise; and what the Rema wrote that it is a matter that is not applicable — he challenged from daf 5 — and one may distinguish: in my opinion there is no need for distinction, for are precise or imprecise from this uncertainty — it is not from uncertainty but thus the Sages enacted that at the beginning of the enactment they enacted everywhere to be stringent — this is its measure in imprecise and in precise; but where there is uncertainty then it is an eruv uncertainty and valid, so what I answered:
5:_: (There in seif 40) A mavo whose one side is long and one short. Behold I was asked regarding a fence enclosed on four sides breached at a corner like the shape of a gimmel on this side and on that side in a manner that if the breach is measured equally — part of this side and part of that side would be more than ten — but if measured diagonally the breach would be only ten or less — how do we measure this, whether its law is as a breach more than ten or less; also whether we measure the diagonal or equally opposite the short side to the wall opposite it so it is less than the length of the diagonal; and this is what I answered: behold in my opinion the matter is clear that we measure the diagonal and it is proved from the Talmud Eruvin daf 8 from which is the source of seif 40 here, and thus it states: Rav Kahana said, etc., a mavo whose one side is long and one short — less than four amot he places the korah diagonally; four amot — he does not place the korah except opposite the short, etc.; Rav Kahana said since you heard the teaching of Kahana I will say a matter: that which you said he places the korah diagonally — we only said when there is not more than ten in its diagonal; but if there is more than ten in its diagonal — he does not place except opposite the short, etc.; and Rashi explained but if there is more than ten in its diagonal — it turns out its opening is wide more than ten for behold all beneath the korah is opening, see there — if so it is proved from this that with diagonal we measure; and even if equally opposite the short there would be only ten we measure specifically in the diagonal; and if so it is proved that with diagonal we measure and even if equally opposite the short there would be only ten; and one cannot say it is different there for it deals only regarding using beneath the korah — this is not so, for behold Taz wrote here that also regarding using within the mavo it is forbidden if it is more than ten in the diagonal — it is proved that also regarding using within the mavo we measure in the diagonal and if it is more than ten the korah does not help — if so it is proved that also regarding using within the mavo we measure in the diagonal; thus it appeared at first glance; however when we examine this it is not so, for this deals entirely when he wishes to place the korah diagonally — since he wishes to use diagonally and make the opening be diagonally the law of opening applies to it — then we measure the measure according to how it is in the diagonal since he wishes to use now the place of the long side and places the korah thus since it equals an opening diagonally — here we measure according to how it is wide in the diagonal; but if he wishes to place the korah opposite the short equally — we measure in truth the opening according to its width equally; if so regarding courtyard it appears since we hold its breach is in ten amot and in less than ten amot no correction is needed at all — it appears the same here; and as the law in mavo through korah — so the law in courtyard by itself to use opposite the long is forbidden if it is more than ten in the diagonal; but opposite the short it is permitted to use even though it is more in the diagonal since equally there are not ten amot — thus it appears to me correct and clear for practical law:
6:_: (There in seif 36 in the gloss) And with this the mound counts as a partition. See in Magen Avraham what is written — it is possible it is not called that the public penetrated it less than sixty myriads as is written in siman 345 seif 7; and it is difficult for me, for behold from Rashi and Magen Avraham below siman 365 s.k. 4 what is written that the public did not penetrate it — meaning such as where there is excrement or mud and filth that it is not the way of the public to pass there — it implies explicitly that specifically where the place is not fit to pass from itself this is not called the public penetrated it; but whatever the place is fit from itself to pass — even though the public did not actually pass there it is called the public penetrated it; and all the more if the public actually penetrated it — only they did not pass sixty myriads — it is called the public penetrated it since the hindrance is not from the place; and behold the main proof of Magen Avraham is from siman 345 that Rashi holds there is no reshut ha-rabbim less than sixty myriads and this is Rashi's view — thus; and from Rashi's words it is proved to the contrary that we do not require sixty myriads — for if so he should have explained plainly that the public did not penetrate it — that they did not pass sixty myriads; and perforce we do not require passing sixty myriads in it but whatever is fit to pass there is called the public penetrated it; and it is possible Magen Avraham distinguishes between this law and there — for there it deals with a mavo corrected with lechi and korah — since the concern there is lest they abandon the large opening and enter through the small opening and nullify the mavo correction — here whatever opening is fit for the public to pass there is this decree; therefore we require specifically excrement and mud, etc.; but where the city is enclosed by partitions like a wall and the like which is full reshut ha-yachid and the Sages did not permit through their decree to nullify the path from the category of reshut ha-yachid — it is not nullified until the public actually penetrated it — specifically sixty myriads; however this is not to examine Tur in this siman that wrote the mound rises in place of lechi — it implies that also with the mound it is from the reason of lechi and automatically whatever is fit to be the public penetrated it the lechi is nullified as is written above — and it is proved from the poskim mentioned that not like Magen Avraham, examine well; and behold the measure of the width of the path that the public penetrated it — we require that it be more than ten amot; but in less than ten amot there is no concern as is proved below in siman 365 and in the Talmud source of the law there; and it is true that from the language of the Shulchan Aruch that wrote there its measure implies the intent is ten tefachim everywhere — for regarding amot it always stated ten amot or simply ten feminine remembering always regarding tefachim; nevertheless perforce the Shulchan Aruch was not precise in language and there the intent is on ten amot as is proved from the Talmud that the matter depends on whether it is measure of an opening or not and measure of opening is always in ten amot — and perforce the Mechaber was not precise in his language; if so with the mound we require that the place where the public penetrated it be more than ten amot and in any case it appears not like Magen Avraham and with this we do not require sixty myriads and it is not similar to the law in siman 345 — for there it speaks regarding the law of full reshut ha-rabbim from the Torah therefore Rashi holds we require sixty myriads; but here for our law we do not require sixty myriads for it is less than sixty myriads it is not reshut ha-rabbim but at least karmelit; and rabbinically we do not require sixty myriads and even in less the partition is nullified; also one may say Rashi's intent there is specifically where there are not sixty myriads at all then it is not reshut ha-rabbim; but here where there are sixty myriads even though in that path they did not penetrate sixty myriads — as long as in the body of the city there are sixty myriads and in that mound the public penetrated it — the partition is nullified; also one may say here it is different for behold if there were no mound they would be forbidden to carry there and would be judged as the public — only through the mound they come to make it reshut ha-rabbim — whatever the public penetrates in the measure that if those public were in a place where there is no mound they would forbid each other — here too the partition is nullified and it has the law of the public penetrated it and the public's penetration operates at least to make the mound partitions as if they do not exist; and if there were no mound there they would certainly be forbidden — here too they are forbidden unlike Rashi's case where it is not from the reason of partition that he permits but that in less than sixty myriads it is not reshut ha-rabbim — here it is permitted in less than sixty myriads; but whatever without the partition would be forbidden — only through the partition they are permitted — whatever the public penetrates that would forbid if there were no mound or partition — also now they nullify the partition;
